steps.say: A shape has rotational symmetry if it looks exactly the same after you turn it by less than a full turn about its centre.
The order of rotational symmetry is the number of different positions in one full turn in which the shape looks the same.
A square looks the same four times in a full turn, at quarter, half and three-quarter turns and back at the start. Its order is 4.
A rectangle that is not a square looks the same after a half turn, so its order is 2. An equilateral triangle has order 3.
A shape that only looks the same after a full turn has order 1. That means no rotational symmetry.

check.prompt: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a square?
hints: Turn a square a quarter turn.
It looks the same after each quarter turn.
Count the quarter turns in a full turn.
check.explanation: A square looks the same four times in a full turn, so its order is 4.

check.prompt: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a rectangle that is not a square?
hints: Turn it a quarter turn. Does it look the same?
It looks the same after a half turn.
Count the positions in a full turn.
check.explanation: A rectangle looks the same after a half turn and a full turn, so its order is 2.
